transcript.content: Hello. Welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Ever since the car accident two weeks ago, I just can’t think straight or focus long enough to finish anything, even simple tasks at work. My mind just goes completely blank when I try to do my job, and my manager is starting to notice how much I'm struggling.
Did you hit your head or lose consciousness during the accident, and have you experienced other physical symptoms like headaches or dizziness since then?

No, I didn't lose consciousness, and I luckily only had some minor physical injuries from the crash. As for headaches or dizziness, I'm not really sure or haven't really noticed having anything like that.
Have you been experiencing any emotional changes since the accident, such as feeling unusually anxious, down, or easily irritated?

Yes, I've been incredibly easily irritated lately, snapping at my sister and coworkers over tiny things and raising my voice before I even realize it. I'm also feeling so anxious that my heart starts racing and my chest gets tight whenever I think about being in a car or when pictures of the crash pop into my head.
Are you actively trying to avoid driving, riding in cars, or thinking about the accident, and have you been having nightmares or trouble sleeping since it happened?

Yes, I've been going way out of my way to avoid that intersection, and I make excuses to avoid driving or riding in cars at night because it makes my chest tighten. I haven't really had nightmares, but those pictures of the crash constantly pop into my head during the day and make it impossible to relax.
Since the accident, have you felt constantly on guard, unusually jumpy, or easily startled by sudden noises or movements?

Yes, I've been incredibly jumpy and easily startled ever since the accident. If someone drops a hanger in the stockroom or a car honks outside, I literally jump out of my skin and my whole body jerks. My heart starts pounding immediately, and it takes me a really long time to calm back down.
Since the accident, have you felt emotionally numb, or detached and distant from your friends and family? Do you find it hard to feel positive emotions like happiness or love?

I wouldn't say I feel completely emotionally numb or unable to feel love. However, I have been withdrawing and bailing on family gatherings lately, mostly because I just feel too overwhelmed to be around people right now.

When those pictures of the crash pop into your head, do you ever feel as though you are actually back at the scene reliving the accident in real-time, temporarily losing touch with your current surroundings?

Yes, when those images pop up, my heart starts racing and it feels intensely like I'm right back in the driver's seat of the car, unable to stop it. Other times, I'll completely space out and feel like I'm watching my own life like a movie, totally disconnected from my body and my surroundings.
Have these symptoms been present nearly every day since the accident, and have you noticed any gradual improvement, or have they remained just as intense?

Yes, they started right after the accident two weeks ago and have been happening constantly every single day. They haven't gotten any better at all and remain just as intense, which makes it really hard to get through my daily life.
During the car accident, did you feel an intense fear for your life, or did you believe that you or someone else was in danger of being seriously injured or killed?

Yes, it was incredibly terrifying and I honestly thought I might die. I was trapped in the car after it got T-boned, surrounded by shattered glass and the smell of burning rubber, panicking that the car would catch fire before help arrived. I was so scared that I was seriously injured and wouldn't make it out alive.
Have you ever experienced any other highly traumatic or life-threatening events in your past, and did you have similar symptoms after those events?
No, I've never experienced any other major traumatic events in my life before this. I have also never had symptoms like this before the accident happened.
Since the accident, have you found yourself holding persistent negative beliefs about yourself or the world, such as feeling that you are permanently ruined or that no place is safe anymore?
No, I haven't really had those specific thoughts. I don't feel like I'm permanently ruined or that the world is completely unsafe.
Have you been experiencing any specific trouble falling asleep or staying asleep since the accident occurred?

No, I haven't really had any specific trouble falling or staying asleep since the accident. It's more that I just can't seem to relax during the day because of the constant memories popping into my head.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1) following a life-threatening motor vehicle accident two weeks ago. The patient experienced a qualifying traumatic stressor (being trapped in a T-boned car with a fear of dying) and presents with a characteristic symptom profile including intrusive memories, physiological reactivity, flashbacks (reliving the event), avoidance of trauma-related stimuli (driving, the crash intersection), hyperarousal (exaggerated startle response, irritability, concentration difficulties), and dissociative symptoms (depersonalization). These symptoms cause significant functional impairment in both occupational and social domains.
